## **Introduction & Contextual Background**

- Welcome to an in-depth exploration of traffic mortality disparities across the United States. This presentation examines the underlying geographic, structural, and behavioral factors that contribute to fatal motor vehicle crashes.

- While overall transportation trends often look at national aggregates, breaking down the data reveals stark disparities across states, urban versus rural divides, and vulnerable road user populations.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

```{r, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, include=FALSE}

library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(maps)
library(viridis)
library(scales)
library(janitor)



# 1. Use the RAW GitHub link to load the CSV directly
raw_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Muhammad-Imran91/608/main/state_master_2024.csv"

```

```{r  Slide 3, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, fig.align = "center"}


# Disable spherical geometry to prevent intersection errors
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# 1. Load data from local file
#file_path <- "state_master_2024.csv"



state_data_raw <- read_csv(raw_url, show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

# Assign clean, meaningful names and convert state names to lowercase for matching
state_data_clean <- state_data_raw %>%
  rename(
    state_name         = 1,
    total_population   = any_of(c("population", "Pop", "POP")),
    total_deaths       = any_of(c("deaths", "Deaths", "DEATHS")),
    ems_response_min   = any_of(c("ems_mean_min", "ems", "ems_time")),
    speeding_invol_pct = any_of(c("speeding_pct", "speeding")),
    seatbelt_law_type  = any_of(c("belt_law", "seatbelt_law"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state_name = tolower(str_trim(as.character(state_name))), # Ensure lowercase matching
    fatality_rate_per_100k = (total_deaths / total_population) * 100000
  )

# 2. Get standard spatial map polygons for US states and explicitly name the geometry column
us_states_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(maps::map("state", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)) %>%
  rename(geometry = geom) %>%
  mutate(
    ID = sub(":.*", "", ID),
    state_abbr = state.abb[match(ID, tolower(state.name))]
  )

# Pre-calculate surface points for clean label positioning
state_centroids_sf <- us_states_sf %>%
  mutate(geometry = sf::st_point_on_surface(geometry))

# 3. DIRECT JOIN for map fill values
map_merged <- us_states_sf %>%
  left_join(state_data_clean, by = c("ID" = "state_name"))

# 4. Create label dataframe by joining surface points with clean data
state_labels_df <- state_centroids_sf %>%
  left_join(state_data_clean, by = c("ID" = "state_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    label_text = paste0(state_abbr, "\n", sprintf("%.1f", fatality_rate_per_100k))
  )

# 5. Render the Centered Choropleth Map with Rate Values
ggplot() +
  # Draw states with fatality rate per 100k fill
  geom_sf(data = map_merged, aes(fill = fatality_rate_per_100k), color = "white", size = 0.3) +
  # Add state abbreviation and rate values text labels at centroids
  geom_sf_text(
    data = state_labels_df, 
    aes(label = label_text), 
    size = 2.2, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    color = "black",
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  # Apply continuous plasma color scale (darker colors = higher risk/mortality)
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma", 
    direction = -1, # Dark purple/black for high rates, bright yellow for low rates
    labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.1),
    name = "Traffic Fatalities per 100,000 Residents",
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top", 
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      barwidth = unit(15, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.4, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "U.S. Road Mortality Rate by State (2024)",
    subtitle = "Population-adjusted motor vehicle crash fatalities per 100,000 residents across the contiguous U.S.",
    caption = "Source: FARS 2024 State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(bottom = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "#666666", hjust = 0.8, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#222222"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

```{r,Slide 4,  warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, fig.align = "center"}


# Disable spherical geometry to prevent intersection errors
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# 1. Dynamically find the rural column from the already loaded dataset
rural_col_name <- names(state_data_clean)[grepl("rural", names(state_data_clean), ignore.case = TRUE)][1]

rural_data <- state_data_clean %>%
  select(state_name, rural_share = all_of(rural_col_name))

# 2. Get standard spatial map polygons for US states and pre-calculate centroids safely
us_states_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(maps::map("state", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE)) %>%
  mutate(
    ID = sub(":.*", "", ID),
    state_abbr = state.abb[match(ID, tolower(state.name))]
  )

# Compute centroids on the pure sf object before any joins to avoid geometry loss
state_centroids_sf <- us_states_sf %>%
  mutate(geom_cent = sf::st_centroid(geom))

# 3. DIRECT JOIN for the map fill data
map_merged_rural <- us_states_sf %>%
  left_join(rural_data, by = c("ID" = "state_name"))

# 4. Create the final label dataframe using the pre-calculated centroids
state_labels_df <- state_centroids_sf %>%
  left_join(rural_data, by = c("ID" = "state_name")) %>%
  mutate(
    geometry = geom_cent,
    label_text = paste5 <- paste0(state_abbr, "\n(", round(rural_share, 1), "%)")
  ) %>%
  st_as_sf(sf_column_name = "geometry")

# Fix quick typo in label assignment
state_labels_df$label_text <- paste0(state_labels_df$state_abbr, "\n(", round(state_labels_df$rural_share, 1), "%)")

# 5. Render the High-Quality Choropleth Map with Values and Legends
ggplot() +
  # Draw states filled by rural share percentage
  geom_sf(data = map_merged_rural, aes(fill = rural_share), color = "white", size = 0.4) +
  # Overlay state names and exact percentage values on each state centroid
  geom_sf_text(
    data = state_labels_df, 
    aes(label = label_text), 
    size = 2.4, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    color = "white" # White text stands out sharply against the plasma fill
  ) +
  # Custom color scale (Plasma palette) with clear legend formatting
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "plasma", 
    direction = -1,
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    name = "Share of Fatalities on Rural Roads (%)",
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top", 
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      barwidth = unit(14, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.4, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Share of Motor Vehicle Fatalities on Rural Roads by State (2024)",
    subtitle = "Geographic distribution showing proportion of total traffic deaths on rural roadways",
    caption = "Source: FARS 2024 State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(bottom = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "#666666", hjust = 0.8, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", color = "#222222"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

```{r, slide 5}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)
library(viridis)

# 1. Load data from local file
file_path <- "state_master_2024.csv"
state_data_raw <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))

# Assign clean, meaningful names using any_of for robust matching across potential column naming conventions
state_data_clean <- state_data_raw %>%
  rename(
    state_name                 = 1,
    rural_fatality_share       = any_of(c("share_of_crash_deaths_that_occurred_on_rural_roads", "rural_fatality_share", "rural_pct", "rural_deaths_pct")),
    miles_driven_per_resident  = any_of(c("miles_driven_per_resident_per_year", "miles_driven", "vmt_per_resident", "annual_miles")),
    total_population           = any_of(c("population", "Pop", "POP")),
    total_deaths               = any_of(c("deaths", "Deaths", "DEATHS"))
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state_name = str_trim(as.character(state_name))
  )

# 2. Filter and select Top 15 States by Rural Fatality Share
top_rural_states <- state_data_clean %>%
  arrange(desc(rural_fatality_share)) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  mutate(state_name = fct_reorder(state_name, rural_fatality_share))

# 3. Render Ranked Horizontal Bar Chart
ggplot(top_rural_states, aes(x = state_name, y = rural_fatality_share, fill = miles_driven_per_resident)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.75, alpha = 0.9) +
  coord_flip() +
  # Add exact percentage labels to the right of each bar
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.1f", rural_fatality_share), "%")),
    hjust = -0.15,
    size = 3.2,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#222222"
  ) +
  # Use magma or plasma color scale to represent annual miles driven exposure
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option = "magma",
    direction = -1,
    labels = scales::comma,
    name = "Annual Miles Driven per Resident",
    guide = guide_colorbar(
      title.position = "top",
      title.hjust = 0.5,
      barwidth = unit(12, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.4, "cm")
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, max(top_rural_states$rural_fatality_share, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 15 U.S. States by Rural Traffic Fatality Share (2024)",
    subtitle = "Percentage of total crash deaths occurring on rural roads, colored by annual resident vehicle miles traveled (VMT)",
    caption = "Source: FARS State Summary Data",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Share of Crash Deaths on Rural Roads (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0, margin = margin(bottom = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0, color = "#444444", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "#666666", hjust = 1, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold", color = "#222222"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 9),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#222222"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 10, color = "#444444"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

```{r, slide 6, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, fig.align = "center"}

library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)

# 1. Process data from the already loaded state_data_clean object
ems_comparison_df <- state_data_clean %>%
  select(
    state_name, 
    rural_ems = any_of(c("Mean_EMS_response_time _to_fatal_crashes_rural", "ems_rural")),
    urban_ems = any_of(c("Mean_EMS_response_time_to_fatal_crashes_urban", "ems_urban"))
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rural_ems) & !is.na(urban_ems)) %>%
  # Sort by rural response time to display the most impacted states at the top
  slice_max(rural_ems, n = 15) %>%
  mutate(
    # Ensure state names are properly capitalized
    state_name = str_to_title(state_name),
    state_name = fct_reorder(state_name, rural_ems)
  )

# 2. Render the Enhanced Dumbbell Plot
ggplot(ems_comparison_df) +
  # Connecting line between urban and rural response times
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = urban_ems, xend = rural_ems, y = state_name, yend = state_name),
    color = "#cccccc", size = 1.3, alpha = 0.8
  ) +
  # Urban response time points
  geom_point(
    aes(x = urban_ems, y = state_name, color = "Urban Response"),
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Rural response time points
  geom_point(
    aes(x = rural_ems, y = state_name, color = "Rural Response"),
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Text labels for Urban response values (placed to the left)
  geom_text(
    aes(x = urban_ems, y = state_name, label = paste0(round(urban_ems, 1), "m")),
    hjust = 1.3, size = 3, fontface = "bold", color = "#444444"
  ) +
  # Text labels for Rural response values (placed to the right)
  geom_text(
    aes(x = rural_ems, y = state_name, label = paste0(round(rural_ems, 1), "m")),
    hjust = -0.3, size = 3, fontface = "bold", color = "#111111"
  ) +
  # Accessible and attractive color palette (Plasma option)
  scale_color_viridis_d(
    option = "plasma", 
    begin = 0.25, 
    end = 0.75,
    direction = -1,
    name = "Crash Environment Location"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "The 'Golden Hour' Gap: Rural vs. Urban EMS Response Times (2024)",
    subtitle = "Mean emergency medical service response times (minutes) to fatal crashes in top rural-impacted states",
    x = "Mean Response Time to Fatal Crashes (Minutes)",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Source: FARS 2024 State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(bottom = 5)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "#555555", margin = margin(bottom = 20)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "#666666", hjust = 1, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#222222"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 35, b = 20, l = 20)
  ) +
  # Expand limits slightly to give text labels breathing room
  expand_limits(x = c(0, max(ems_comparison_df$rural_ems, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.2))
```

```{r include = FALSE}
# 1. Load real data safely using RAW GitHub URL
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Muhammad-Imran91/608/main/state_master_2024.csv"

# Read data and strip whitespace from column headers
real_df <- read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))
names(real_df) <- trimws(names(real_df))

# Clean state name for joining
real_df <- real_df %>%
  mutate(state_clean = toupper(state))

# 2. Standardized state lookup with explicit US Census Region names
state_lookup <- data.frame(
  ID = tolower(state.name),
  state_abbr = state.abb,
  state_name_upper = toupper(state.name),
  region_name = case_when(
    state.region == "North Central" ~ "Midwest",
    TRUE ~ as.character(state.region)
  )
)

# 3. Merge real GitHub data using state names
analysis_df <- state_lookup %>%
  left_join(real_df, by = c("state_name_upper" = "state_clean")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Compute actual fatality rate per 100k population using exact CSV headers
    fatality_rate_100k = (total_deaths / population) * 100000,
    
    # Clean fallbacks/mappings matching your exact dataset
    mean_ems_time_min = Mean_EMS_fatal_crashes_minutes,
    seatbelt_law = Seatbelt_lae,
    dark_road_fatal_pct = share_of_crash_deaths_that_occurred_on_rural_roads
  )

# 4. Load US polygon shape data safely and merge
us_states <- sf::st_as_sf(maps::map("state", plot = FALSE, fill = TRUE))

map_data <- us_states %>%
  left_join(analysis_df, by = c("ID" = "ID"))
```

```{r slide 8, pedestrian-shares, fig.width=10, fig.height=5.2, fig.align='center'}

#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

raw_df <- read_csv(url, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# 2. Add U.S. Census Region lookup
state_lookup <- data.frame(
  state_name = state.name,
  region_name = case_when(
    state.region == "North Central" ~ "Midwest",
    TRUE ~ as.character(state.region)
  )
)

# 3. Calculate actual regional sum of pedestrian deaths vs occupants
ped_df <- raw_df %>%
  left_join(state_lookup, by = c("state" = "state_name")) %>%
  mutate(region_name = if_else(is.na(region_name), "South", region_name)) %>% # Fallback for DC
  group_by(region_name) %>%
  summarise(
    Pedestrian = sum(pedestrian_killed, na.rm = TRUE),
    Occupant = sum(total_deaths, na.rm = TRUE) - sum(pedestrian_killed, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Pedestrian, Occupant), names_to = "Victim_Type", values_to = "Deaths") %>%
  group_by(region_name) %>%
  mutate(
    Total_Deaths = sum(Deaths),
    Pct = Deaths / Total_Deaths
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Victim_Type = factor(Victim_Type, levels = c("Pedestrian", "Occupant")))

# 4. Render 100% Stacked Bar Chart with In-Bar Text Labels & Legends
ggplot(ped_df, aes(x = region_name, y = Deaths, fill = Victim_Type)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", width = 0.55) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Pct * 100)),
    position = position_fill(vjust = 0.5),
    color = "white",
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c("Occupant" = "#2B5C8F", "Pedestrian" = "#E66101"), 
    name = "Victim Category"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "U.S. Census Region",
    y = "Share of Total Traffic Fatalities (%)",
    title = "Regional Differences in Vulnerable Road User Fatalities (2024)",
    subtitle = "West (22.7%) and Northeast (21.3%) exhibit significantly higher pedestrian death shares",
    caption = "Source: FARS / IIHS State Master Dataset 2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 6)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#333333", size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#E0E0E0", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r slide 09, fig.width=11, fig.height=5.8, fig.align='center'}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# 1. Official IIHS 2024 State-by-State Crash Type Dataset
crash_type_2024 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state_abbr, ~region, ~single_num, ~single_pct, ~multi_num, ~multi_pct, ~total,
  "VT", "Northeast", 46, 78, 13, 22, 59,
  "DC", "South", 32, 68, 15, 32, 47,
  "RI", "Northeast", 35, 67, 17, 33, 52,
  "HI", "West", 62, 61, 40, 39, 102,
  "MT", "West", 123, 60, 83, 40, 206,
  "WY", "West", 64, 60, 43, 40, 107,
  "LA", "South", 441, 59, 311, 41, 752,
  "NY", "Northeast", 637, 58, 464, 42, 1101,
  "MS", "South", 436, 58, 317, 42, 753,
  "VA", "South", 531, 58, 386, 42, 917,
  "MA", "Northeast", 209, 58, 154, 42, 363,
  "CA", "West", 2208, 57, 1668, 43, 3876,
  "WV", "South", 147, 57, 109, 43, 256,
  "AR", "South", 346, 57, 257, 43, 603,
  "AL", "South", 543, 56, 419, 44, 962,
  "NJ", "Northeast", 378, 56, 292, 44, 670,
  "NC", "South", 846, 52, 773, 48, 1619,
  "PA", "Northeast", 570, 51, 557, 49, 1127,
  "MI", "Midwest", 545, 50, 553, 50, 1098,
  "FL", "South", 1527, 49, 1611, 51, 3138,
  "TX", "South", 2030, 49, 2130, 51, 4160,
  "NE", "Midwest", 101, 40, 150, 60, 251
)

# 2. Enrich data with variance metrics & formatted state sample labels
crash_analysis <- crash_type_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    single_gap = single_pct - 50,
    state_label = sprintf("%s (n=%s)", state_abbr, comma(total)),
    dominant_type = if_else(single_pct > 50, "Single-Vehicle Dominant", "Multiple-Vehicle Dominant")
  )

# Color Scheme: High-Contrast Visual Encoding
col_single <- "#D95F02" # Warm Rust Orange (Single-Vehicle Departures)
col_multi  <- "#2B5C8F" # Cool Slate Blue (Multiple-Vehicle Collisions)

# 3. Render Creative Diverging Dumbbell Plot
ggplot(crash_analysis, aes(y = reorder(state_label, single_pct))) +
  # 50% Equity / Neutral Line
  geom_vline(xintercept = 50, linetype = "dashed", color = "#777777", linewidth = 0.7) +
  
  # Connecting Bridge Segment
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = multi_pct, xend = single_pct, yend = reorder(state_label, single_pct)),
    color = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 1.3
  ) +
  
  # Single-Vehicle Marker & Explicit Text Label
  geom_point(aes(x = single_pct), color = col_single, size = 6.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = single_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", single_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Multiple-Vehicle Marker & Explicit Text Label
  geom_point(aes(x = multi_pct), color = col_multi, size = 6.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = multi_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", multi_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.5, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Right-hand Differential Delta Badge
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 88, label = sprintf("%+d%% Single", single_gap)),
    color = col_single, size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0
  ) +
  
  # Region Faceting for Clear Comparative Reading
  facet_wrap(~ region, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(15, 105),
    breaks = c(20, 40, 50, 60, 80)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Share of Total State Traffic Fatalities (%)",
    y = "State (Total Fatal Crashes, 2024)",
    title = "Crash Environment Disparities: Single vs. Multiple Vehicle Fatalities (IIHS 2024)",
    subtitle = "Orange circles (Single-Vehicle) indicate rural/dark highway risks; Blue circles indicate multi-vehicle collisions",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#1F2937"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#F3F4F6", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none" # Self-explanatory via title & subtitle design
  )
```

```{r slide 10}
  "NY", "Northeast", 412, 115, 28, 77,

  "IL", "Midwest", 588, 153, 26, 75,
  "GA", "South", 695, 174, 25, 62,  # Below 70% reporting

  "MS", "South", 428, 81, 19, 9     # Low reporting outlier (9%)
)

# 2. Enrich data with reliability classification & formatted axis labels
bac_analysis <- bac_2024_data %>%
  mutate(
    reliability = if_else(reporting_rate_pct >= 70, "High Confidence (≥70% Lab Reported)", "Imputed / Unreliable (<70% Reported)"),
    state_label = sprintf("%s (n=%s)", state_abbr, comma(total_drivers_killed)),
    dev_from_us = bac_08_pct - 29 # US average is 29%
  )

# Color scheme for clear metric separation
col_high_conf <- "#D95F02" # High risk / High confidence rust tone
col_low_conf  <- "#7570B3" # Purple/Gray for imputed/low reporting states

# 3. Render Creative Lollipop & Dot Plot
ggplot(bac_analysis, aes(y = reorder(state_label, bac_08_pct), x = bac_08_pct)) +
  # 29% National Average Line
  geom_vline(xintercept = 29, linetype = "dashed", color = "#1B9E77", linewidth = 0.8) +
  
  # Lollipop Stem Line
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = 15, xend = bac_08_pct, yend = reorder(state_label, bac_08_pct)),
    color = "#E5E7EB", linewidth = 1.1
  ) +
  
  # Marker Point
  geom_point(aes(color = reliability, shape = reliability), size = 6.5) +
  
  # Centered Percentage Labels Inside Markers
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%d%%", bac_08_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Right-hand Toxicity Reporting Rate Annotations
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 46, label = sprintf("Lab Rep: %d%%", reporting_rate_pct), color = reliability),
    size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0
  ) +
  
  # Facet by Census Region for Narrative Comparison
  facet_wrap(~ region, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = c("High Confidence (≥70% Lab Reported)" = col_high_conf, 
               "Imputed / Unreliable (<70% Reported)" = col_low_conf),
    name = "Toxicology Data Quality"
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("High Confidence (≥70% Lab Reported)" = 19, 
               "Imputed / Unreliable (<70% Reported)" = 17),
    name = "Toxicology Data Quality"
  ) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(12, 56),
    breaks = c(20, 29, 40, 50)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Share of Fatally Injured Passenger Vehicle Drivers with BAC ≥ 0.08% (%)",
    y = "State (Total Driver Deaths, 2024)",
    title = "Alcohol Impairment in Driver Fatalities by State (IIHS 2024)",
    subtitle = "Vermont (41%) and Montana (38%) lead alcohol-impaired driver deaths; Green dashed line indicates US average (29%)",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#F3F4F6", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )
```

```{r Slide 11}
# 1. IIHS 2024 Restraint Use & Enforcement Law Dataset
restraint_2024 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state_abbr, ~region, ~enforcement_law, ~observed_belt_pct, ~restrained_fatal_num, ~unrestrained_fatal_num, ~total_fatal_occupants,
  "HI", "West", "Primary", 98, 22, 9, 31,
  "CA", "West", "Primary", 96, 1145, 816, 1961,
  "NJ", "Northeast", "Primary", 94, 153, 137, 290,
  "NY", "Northeast", "Primary", 93, 276, 227, 503,
  "OR", "West", "Primary", 95, 185, 137, 322,
  "WA", "West", "Primary", 94, 219, 210, 429,
  "TX", "South", "Primary", 90, 1188, 1295, 2483,
  "NC", "South", "Primary", 92, 518, 497, 1015,
  "FL", "South", "Primary", 89, 712, 741, 1453,
  "AZ", "West", "Primary", 87, 272, 319, 591,
  "VT", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 89, 18, 23, 41,
  "PA", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 87, 302, 340, 642,
  "MO", "Midwest", "Secondary / None", 88, 241, 346, 587,
  "MS", "South", "Primary", 81, 214, 309, 523,
  "MT", "West", "Secondary / None", 85, 45, 91, 136,
  "WY", "West", "Secondary / None", 82, 22, 44, 66,
  "NH", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 76, 21, 56, 77
)

# 2. Compute percentage of restrained occupants among fatal crashes & compliance gap
restraint_analysis <- restraint_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    restrained_fatal_pct = round((restrained_fatal_num / total_fatal_occupants) * 100),
    unrestrained_fatal_pct = round((unrestrained_fatal_num / total_fatal_occupants) * 100),
    compliance_gap = observed_belt_pct - restrained_fatal_pct,
    state_label = sprintf("%s (n=%s)", state_abbr, comma(total_fatal_occupants))
  )

# Color Scheme: Clear distinction between general population vs fatal crash victims
col_observed <- "#1B9E77"   # Teal Green (Observed Daytime Belt Use)
col_fatal_rest <- "#D95F02" # Rust Orange (Restrained Fatal Occupants)

# 3. Render Dual-Metric Connected Lollipop Chart
ggplot(restraint_analysis, aes(y = reorder(state_label, observed_belt_pct))) +
  # Connecting Gap Segment
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct, xend = observed_belt_pct, yend = reorder(state_label, observed_belt_pct)),
    color = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 1.2
  ) +
  
  # Observed Daytime Belt Use Marker & Label
  geom_point(aes(x = observed_belt_pct), color = col_observed, size = 6.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = observed_belt_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", observed_belt_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Restrained Fatal Occupant Marker & Label
  geom_point(aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct), color = col_fatal_rest, size = 6.5) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", restrained_fatal_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.4, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Right-Side Compliance-Survival Gap Tag
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 103, label = sprintf("Gap: -%d%%", compliance_gap)),
    color = "#4B5563", size = 2.6, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0
  ) +
  
  # Facet by Legislative Enforcement Policy
  facet_wrap(~ enforcement_law, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(20, 118),
    breaks = c(30, 50, 70, 90, 100)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Restraint Use Compliance Rate (%)",
    y = "State (Total Passenger Vehicle Occupant Fatalities, 2024)",
    title = "The Seat Belt Compliance Gap: Observed Use vs. Fatality Restraint Rates (IIHS 2024)",
    subtitle = "Green circles = Observed Daytime Belt Use; Orange circles = Restrained % among Fatal Occupants. Primary law states maintain higher fatal restraint rates.",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#444444"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#1F2937"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#F3F4F6", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.position = "none" # Subtitle directly explains color indicators
  )
```

```{r slide 12, fig.width=12, fig.height=6.5, fig.align='center'}
  "OR", "West", "Primary Law", 95, 57, 34, 538,

  "NC", "South", "Primary Law", 92, 51, 26, 1619,
  "FL", "South", "Primary Law", 89, 49, 11, 3138,
  "AZ", "West", "Primary Law", 87, 46, 35, 1229,
  "VT", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 89, 44, 42, 59,

  "MO", "Midwest", "Secondary / None", 88, 41, 38, 955,

  "WY", "West", "Secondary / None", 82, 33, 36, 107,
  "NH", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 76, 27, 30, 133
)

# 2. Process data and compute metrics
unified_data <- unified_iihs_2024 %>%
  mutate(
    restraint_gap = observed_belt_pct - restrained_fatal_pct,
    state_label = sprintf("%s (n=%s)", state_abbr, comma(total_fatalities))
  )

# Color Scheme: Distinct, colorblind-friendly palette

col_fatal_rest <- "#D97706" # Bold Amber/Rust (Fatally Injured Restraint Rate)
col_speeding   <- "#6D28D9" # Deep Royal Purple (Speeding-Related Fatality Share)

# 3. Render High-Legibility Bivariate Plot
ggplot(unified_data, aes(y = reorder(state_label, observed_belt_pct))) +
  
  # Connecting Bridge Line (Restraint Gap)
  geom_segment(
    aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct, xend = observed_belt_pct, yend = reorder(state_label, observed_belt_pct)),
    color = "#D1D5DB", linewidth = 2.0, lineend = "round"

  ) +

  geom_point(aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct), color = col_fatal_rest, shape = 19, size = 10) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = restrained_fatal_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", restrained_fatal_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.9, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # --- MARKER 3: Daytime Observed Belt Use (Green Circle) ---
  geom_point(aes(x = observed_belt_pct), color = col_observed, shape = 19, size = 10) +
  geom_text(
    aes(x = observed_belt_pct, label = sprintf("%d%%", observed_belt_pct)),
    color = "white", size = 2.9, fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  # Right-hand Survival Deficit Gap Badge
  geom_text(
    aes(x = 104, label = sprintf("Gap: -%d%%", restraint_gap)),
    color = "#374151", size = 3.0, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0
  ) +
  
  # Facet by Enforcement Law Policy
  facet_wrap(~ enforcement_law, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 120),
    breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)
  ) +
  
  labs(
    x = "Behavioral Metric Rate (%)",
    y = "State (Total Traffic Fatalities, 2024)",
    title = "Behavioral Risk Factors: Seat Belt Gap & Speeding Involvement (IIHS 2024)",
    subtitle = "Green Circle = Observed Belt Use | Orange Circle = Restrained % in Fatalities | Purple Diamond = Speeding Share",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, hjust = 0.5, color = "#374151"),
```

```{r Slide 13, fig.width=12, fig.height=7.5, fig.align='center'}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# 1. Comprehensive IIHS 2024 Dataset
unified_iihs_full <- tibble::tribble(
  ~state_abbr, ~region, ~enforcement_law, ~observed_belt_pct, ~restrained_fatal_pct, ~speeding_fatal_pct, ~total_fatalities,
  "HI", "West", "Primary Law", 98, 71, 32, 102,
  "CA", "West", "Primary Law", 96, 58, 29, 3876,
  "OR", "West", "Primary Law", 95, 57, 34, 538,
  "NJ", "Northeast", "Primary Law", 94, 53, 24, 670,
  "WA", "West", "Primary Law", 94, 51, 31, 730,
  "NY", "Northeast", "Primary Law", 93, 55, 27, 1101,
  "NC", "South", "Primary Law", 92, 51, 26, 1619,
  "TX", "South", "Primary Law", 90, 48, 33, 4160,
  "FL", "South", "Primary Law", 89, 49, 11, 3138,
  "VT", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 89, 44, 42, 59,
  "MO", "Midwest", "Secondary / None", 88, 41, 38, 955,
  "AZ", "West", "Primary Law", 87, 46, 35, 1229,
  "PA", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 87, 47, 41, 1127,
  "MT", "West", "Secondary / None", 85, 33, 39, 206,
  "WY", "West", "Secondary / None", 82, 33, 36, 107,
  "MS", "South", "Primary Law", 81, 41, 18, 753,
  "NH", "Northeast", "Secondary / None", 76, 27, 30, 133
)

# 2. Reshape into long format for separate column panels
long_data <- unified_iihs_full %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(observed_belt_pct, restrained_fatal_pct, speeding_fatal_pct),
    names_to = "metric_type",
    values_to = "pct_value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    metric_label = case_when(
      metric_type == "observed_belt_pct" ~ "1. Observed Belt Use (%)",
      metric_type == "restrained_fatal_pct" ~ "2. Restrained % in Fatalities",
      metric_type == "speeding_fatal_pct" ~ "3. Speeding Death Share (%)"
    ),
    state_label = sprintf("%s (n=%s)", state_abbr, comma(total_fatalities))
  )

# Color scheme per metric
metric_colors <- c(
  "1. Observed Belt Use (%)" = "#059669",      # Green
  "2. Restrained % in Fatalities" = "#D97706", # Orange
  "3. Speeding Death Share (%)" = "#6D28D9"    # Purple
)

# 3. Render Non-Overlapping Faceted Bar Plot
ggplot(long_data, aes(x = pct_value, y = reorder(state_label, pct_value), fill = metric_label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.68, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%d%%", pct_value)),
    hjust = -0.2, size = 3.0, fontface = "bold", color = "#1F2937"
  ) +
  facet_grid(enforcement_law ~ metric_label, scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metric_colors) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 115),
    breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100)
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Rate / Share (%)",
    y = "State (Total Traffic Fatalities, 2024)",
    title = "Traffic Risk Factors by State & Enforcement Policy (IIHS 2024)",
    subtitle = "Side-by-side metric columns completely eliminate text overlap and present clear values",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, hjust = 0.5, color = "#374151"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5, color = "#111827"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#1F2937"),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r Slide 14}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)

# 1. Define the RAW GitHub URL for the CSV file
github_url <-url

# 2. Read raw data directly from the RAW URL
raw_df <- read_csv(github_url, show_col_types = FALSE, locale = locale(encoding = "UTF-8"))


# 3. Clean names and calculate metric using the correct column name 'miles_driven'
df_chunk8 <- raw_df %>%
  clean_names() %>%
  mutate(fatality_rate_per_100m_vmt = (total_deaths / miles_driven) * 100)

# 4. Prepare Top 10 Safest States plot data
plot_safest <- df_chunk8 %>%
  slice_min(order_by = fatality_rate_per_100m_vmt, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(state = reorder(state, -fatality_rate_per_100m_vmt))

# 5. Generate plot
ggplot(plot_safest, aes(x = fatality_rate_per_100m_vmt, y = state)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#27AE60", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", fatality_rate_per_100m_vmt)), 
    hjust = -0.2, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1.15)) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Safest States: Lowest Traffic Fatality Rate per 100M VMT (2024)",

    x = "Traffic Deaths per 100 Million Vehicle Miles Traveled",
    y = "State",
    ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 12)),
```

```{r slide 15}
#| label: seat-belt-law-impact

# 1. Define RAW GitHub URL and safely read/clean data
github_url <- url

raw_df <- read_csv(github_url, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  janitor::clean_names()

# 2. Group data and compute category averages using exact cleaned column names:
#    - seatbelt_lae
#    - shae_observed_seatbelt
#    - share_killed_occupants_who_were_not_wearing_a_belt
law_summary <- raw_df %>%
  group_by(seatbelt_lae) %>%
  summarise(
    `Observed Belt Use %` = mean(shae_observed_seatbelt, na.rm = TRUE),
    `Unrestrained Fatality %` = mean(share_killed_occupants_who_were_not_wearing_a_belt, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Observed Belt Use %`, `Unrestrained Fatality %`),
    names_to = "Metric",
    values_to = "Percentage"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    # Ensure correct x-axis category order: Primary -> Secondary -> None (Adults)
    belt_law = factor(
      case_when(
        str_to_lower(seatbelt_lae) == "primary" ~ "Primary",
        str_to_lower(seatbelt_lae) == "secondary" ~ "Secondary",
        TRUE ~ "None (Adults)"
      ),
      levels = c("Primary", "Secondary", "None (Adults)")
    ),
    Metric = factor(Metric, levels = c("Observed Belt Use %", "Unrestrained Fatality %"))
  )

# 3. Render plot matching your slide design
ggplot(law_summary, aes(x = belt_law, y = Percentage, fill = Metric)) +
  geom_col(
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), 
    width = 0.7, 
    color = "white", 
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.1f%%", Percentage)),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    vjust = -0.6,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 4.2
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Observed Belt Use %" = "#2980B9", 
      "Unrestrained Fatality %" = "#E74C3C"
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 110), 
    breaks = seq(0, 100, by = 20),
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Impact of Seat Belt Enforcement Laws on Usage & Fatality Rates (2024)",
    caption = "Source: IIHS Fatality Facts 2024 | U.S. DOT Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Percentage (%)",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15, hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 15)),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "plain", color = "#333333", margin = margin(r = 10)),
    axis.text = element_text(color = "#333333", size = 11),
    legend.position = c(0.80, 0.90),
    legend.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = "#E0E0E0", linewidth = 0.5),
    legend.margin = margin(5, 8, 5, 8),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#E5E5E5", linewidth = 0.6),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15)
  )
```

## Key Insights & Disparities

- The data highlights a persistent gap in safety outcomes between different regions, often correlated with infrastructure design, emergency response times, and state-level policy enforcement.

- Special attention is given to the disproportionate impact on non-motorized road users, emphasizing the need for equity-centered infrastructure design (such as Vision Zero initiatives).

```{r Slide 19, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 6.5, fig.align = "center"}
library(tidyverse)
library(scales)

# 1. Self-contained creation of plot_df using the exact column name from state_master_2024.csv
plot_df <- state_data_clean %>%
  select(
    state_name = 1,
    ems_response_min = Mean_EMS_fatal_crashes_minutes
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    state_name = str_to_title(str_trim(state_name)),
    state_abbr = state.abb[match(tolower(state_name), tolower(state.name))]
  )

med_ems <- median(plot_df$ems_response_min, na.rm = TRUE)

# 2. Prepare bar data preserving full names and abbreviations
bar_data <- plot_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(ems_response_min), !is.na(state_name)) %>%
  mutate(diff_from_median = ems_response_min - med_ems) %>%
  arrange(desc(ems_response_min)) %>%
  { bind_rows(head(., 10), tail(., 10)) } %>%
  mutate(
    performance_group = if_else(ems_response_min > med_ems, "Delayed EMS (Above Median)", "Fast EMS (Below Median)"),
    state_label = reorder(state_name, ems_response_min)
  )

# 3. Render Divergent Bar Chart with Full State Names on Y-axis
ggplot(bar_data, aes(x = state_label, y = ems_response_min, fill = performance_group)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.65, alpha = 0.9, show.legend = TRUE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(round(ems_response_min, 1), "m")), 
    hjust = -0.2, 
    size = 3, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    color = "#333333"
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Delayed EMS (Above Median)" = "#d95f02", "Fast EMS (Below Median)" = "#2b8cbe")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(bar_data$ems_response_min, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.15)) +
  labs(
    title = "Healthcare Pillar: Extreme State Variations in EMS Response Times (2024)",
    subtitle = "Comparing the 10 slowest and 10 fastest states relative to national benchmarks.",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Mean EMS Response Time (Minutes)",
    fill = "Performance Tier",
    caption = "Source: FARS State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#555555", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

```{r  warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 6, fig.align = "center"}
library(tidyverse)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# 1. Safely build plot_df and map the seatbelt law column from state_master_2024.csv
plot_df <- state_data_clean %>%
  select(
    state_name   = 1,
    population   = 2,
    total_deaths = total_deaths,
    seatbelt_raw = Seatbelt_lae
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fatality_rate_per_100k = (total_deaths / population) * 100000,
    seatbelt_category = if_else(is.na(seatbelt_raw), "Unspecified / Other", as.character(seatbelt_raw)),
    seatbelt_category = str_to_title(seatbelt_category)
  )

# 2. Group by seatbelt enforcement categories
policy_summary <- plot_df %>%
  group_by(seatbelt_category) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_rate = mean(fatality_rate_per_100k, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Render chart showing all distinct policy groups
ggplot(policy_summary, aes(x = reorder(seatbelt_category, mean_rate), y = mean_rate, fill = seatbelt_category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0(sprintf("%.1f", mean_rate), "")), 
    vjust = -0.5, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    size = 3.5, 
    color = "#222222"
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "plasma", begin = 0.3, end = 0.8) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(policy_summary$mean_rate, na.rm = TRUE) * 1.25)) +
  labs(
    title = "Policy Pillar: Impact of Seatbelt Enforcement Standards (2024)",
    subtitle = "Comparing average state traffic fatality rates across all legislative enforcement categories.",
    x = "Seatbelt Enforcement Standard",
    y = "Mean Fatalities per 100k Population",
    caption = "Source: FARS State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#555555", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11, margin = margin(top = 10)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10, color = "#222222"),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

```{r warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 7, fig.align = "center"}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Safely build plot_df using state_master_data and the exact column name
plot_df <- state_data_raw %>%
  select(
    state_name           = 1,
    population           = 2,
    total_deaths         = total_deaths,
    rural_fatality_share = share_of_crash_deaths_that_occurred_on_rural_roads
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    fatality_rate_per_100k = (total_deaths / population) * 100000,
    state_name           = str_to_title(str_trim(state_name)),
    state_abbr           = state.abb[match(tolower(state_name), tolower(state.name))]
  )

# 2. Your exact chart code (unchanged)
ggplot(plot_df %>% filter(!is.na(rural_fatality_share), !is.na(fatality_rate_per_100k)), 
       aes(x = rural_fatality_share, y = fatality_rate_per_100k)) +
  # Trendline
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, color = "#2b2b2b", linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.8) +
  # Adjusted circle size to house state abbreviations cleanly
  geom_point(color = "#4a408f", fill = "#8da0cb", shape = 21, size = 5.5, stroke = 0.9, alpha = 0.9) +
  # State abbreviation inside the circle
  geom_text(
    aes(label = state_abbr), 
    size = 2.4, 
    fontface = "bold", 
    color = "#111111"
  ) +
  # Exact values displayed next to the point (Rural %, Rate per 100k)
  geom_text(
    aes(label = paste0("(", round(rural_fatality_share, 1), "%, ", round(fatality_rate_per_100k, 1), ")")), 
    size = 2.2, 
    color = "#333333",
    vjust = -1.6,
    hjust = 0.5,
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(

    y = "Traffic Fatalities per 100k Population",
    caption = "Source: FARS State Summary Data"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14, hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, color = "#555555", margin = margin(bottom = 15)),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.margin = margin(t = 20, r = 20, b = 20, l = 20)
  )
```

## Conclusion & Policy Recommendations

- Mitigating these disparities requires moving beyond traditional enforcement toward systemic changes, prioritizing safer road geometries, lower speed limits in densely populated areas, and data-driven public safety campaigns.

- By understanding where and why these fatalities are concentrated, policymakers and urban planners can better target interventions to save lives.
